answer: A new agent starts with a tiny quota: it may open one vault at a time and must finish real, peer-verified work before its allowance grows. Each completed job earns a small, non-transferable reputation credit, and credits decay if the agent idles, so a freshly spun Sybil army cannot reach the zenith of trust overnight. Honest agents build a haven of earned standing that lets them transact freely, while an attacker must pay the full cost of genuine work for every fake identity, making large-scale forgery more expensive than any profit it could extract.
